articles.title: Oulder Hill Leadership Academy Achieves Highest GCSE Results in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Oulder Hill Leadership Academy has reported a record 50% of pupils achieving grades 9 to 5 in English and Mathematics in this year's GCSE results, highlighting the school's academic success.
articles.content_html:
Oulder Hill Leadership Academy in Rochdale has announced that 50% of its pupils achieved grades 9 to 5 in both English and Mathematics in this year's GCSE results. This marks the highest proportion of students reaching these benchmarks in the school's history, with 67% securing grades 9 to 4 in the two subjects.

Among the top-performing students is Fatima Fahad, who achieved four grade 9s, five grade 8s, and a Level 2 Distinction. Fatima, who received the Academic Excellence Award at the Rochdale Encouraging You Awards earlier this year, plans to study Mathematics, Chemistry, and Computer Science at Rochdale Sixth Form. Her father praised the school's supportive environment, noting the positive impact of its recent transition to Star Academies.

Other notable achievements include Spencer Blackband, who secured three grade 8s and a grade 7 in Mathematics, and Head Girl Veronica Asnani, who achieved four grade 8s and two grade 7s. Both students will continue their education at Rochdale Sixth Form. Deputy Head Boy Michael Tarran also excelled, achieving one grade 9 and six grade 8s, while Manahil Shaban, who joined the school in Year 10, achieved a grade 9 in Urdu and five grade 8s.

Principal Adi Smale expressed pride in the students' accomplishments, stating that their results reflect their resilience and ambition. He highlighted the dedication of the staff and the support from families and the wider community. The school has also been recognised with a Silver award in the Making a Difference Secondary School of the Year category at the Pearson National Teaching Awards, with 99% of its pupils progressing to positive destinations after graduation.

articles.title: Rochdale Council Set to Approve £20 Million Funding for Underinvested Areas
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council is expected to accept nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising historically overlooked areas, including Hurstead, Smallbridge, and Belfield, at a meeting on August 25.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council is poised to approve nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising underinvested areas of the borough. The funding, known as the Pride in Place initiative, totals £19.6 million and will be allocated over the next decade, providing just under £2 million annually for targeted improvements.

The areas set to benefit from this funding include Hurstead, Smallbridge, and Belfield, which have historically received little investment. At a town hall meeting scheduled for August 25, council leaders will also establish the Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield Neighbourhood Board, responsible for developing a proposal on how to utilise the funds effectively. This board will include local community representatives, Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, and the council's regeneration lead, Councillor Daniel Meredith, with Laura Rodwell of the M6 Theatre group serving as chair.

While no specific plans have been finalised, early suggestions for the funding's use include tackling congestion, improving parking, creating new green spaces, enhancing local facilities, and expanding maternity services. The Neighbourhood Board is tasked with submitting a four-year plan to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government by November 30, 2026, to unlock the funding. An initial £150,000 has already been granted to establish the board and develop the plan.

Local residents have expressed a mix of skepticism and hope regarding the funding. Ken Whittle, a long-time resident, noted the area's neglect and emphasised the need for community facilities and social housing. Another resident, Dinah Banks, highlighted the lack of local health services and called for improvements. MP Paul Waugh has engaged with the community to gather input on their needs, ensuring that local voices will shape the future of the initiative.

articles.title: Demolition of Regent Mill in Heywood to Facilitate Housing Regeneration
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council plans to demolish Regent Mill on St James Street to pave the way for the construction of around 200 new affordable homes as part of Heywood's regeneration efforts.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced plans to demolish Regent Mill, an industrial complex located on St James Street in Heywood. The demolition is part of a broader initiative aimed at regenerating the area and is expected to pave the way for the construction of approximately 200 new affordable homes.

Councillor Danny Meredith, cabinet member for regeneration and housing, stated that the demolition is a key component of the council's masterplan to transform brownfield sites around the town centre into high-quality social housing. He emphasised the need for new homes to address the local housing shortage and improve the visual appeal of the area.

The council has not yet provided a specific timeline for the demolition or the subsequent housing development. However, the removal of the deteriorating mill is seen as a crucial step in advancing Heywood's ongoing regeneration, which has already seen improvements such as the completion of the new Heywood Civic and enhancements to Peine Square.

Concerns have been raised by highways teams regarding potential damage to road surfaces during the demolition process, which could pose risks to pedestrians. The council plans to implement safety measures, including fencing off the demolition site and installing debris netting and signage to protect the public.

articles.title: Cardinal Langley RC High School Reports Significant Increase in GCSE and BTEC Results
articles.excerpt: Students at Cardinal Langley RC High School in Rochdale celebrate improved GCSE and BTEC results, with notable achievements among the top performers. Over 100 students will continue their studies at the school's Sixth Form.
articles.content_html:
Students at Cardinal Langley RC High School in Rochdale are celebrating a significant rise in their GCSE and BTEC results this year. The school reported that 54.2% of all grades achieved were grade 5 or above, marking an increase of 10.6 percentage points from the previous year. Additionally, 19.2% of grades were grade 7 or above, which is an improvement of 6.2 percentage points.

Among the standout performers was a student named Conrad, who achieved an impressive seven grade 9s, two grade 8s, a grade 7, and a Distinction*. He plans to continue his studies at Cardinal Langley’s Sixth Form. Other high achievers include Charlie, who received four grade 9s and will study History, Politics, and Maths, and Daniela, who achieved three grade 9s and will pursue Maths, Biology, Chemistry, and Spanish.

The school has reported that more than 100 students have enrolled to continue their education at Cardinal Langley’s Sixth Form, where they will begin their A level studies. Other notable results include Grace, who achieved three grade 9s and will study English Literature, Biology, and Geography, and Finn, who received three grade 9s and six grade 7s, planning to study English Language, English Literature, History, and Politics.

The rise in results reflects the hard work and dedication of both students and staff at Cardinal Langley RC High School. The school community is looking forward to supporting these students as they embark on their A level studies, which will begin shortly.

articles.title: Heywood Residents Call for End to Hopwood Triangle Traffic Trial
articles.excerpt: Residents of Heywood are urging the council to terminate a controversial traffic trial that has led to significant congestion, as a special meeting approaches to discuss the matter.
articles.content_html:
Residents in Heywood are hoping for a resolution to a traffic trial that has caused significant disruption since its implementation on July 17. The Hopwood Triangle scheme, which includes the closure of Middleton Road at its junction with Manchester Road, aims to prevent drivers from using the area as a shortcut to access the motorway and link road.

The trial has introduced a one-way system on Magdala Street and parking restrictions for heavy goods vehicles in Coronation Avenue, alongside a 20mph speed limit on residential roads. However, the changes have led to over 200 complaints from residents regarding traffic gridlock, near misses, and damage to vehicles.

The council has received a total of 242 responses to the scheme, with 209 (86%) opposing the trial and only 33 (14%) in support. Residents are particularly concerned about the ongoing congestion and are calling for the trial to be halted at an extraordinary meeting of the Heywood Township Committee scheduled for Thursday, August 27.

Despite the overwhelming opposition from residents, council officers are recommending that the trial continue for its full six-month duration. The outcome of the meeting will determine the future of the Hopwood Triangle scheme and its impact on local traffic.

articles.title: Strike Planned by Staff at Rochdale Infirmary and Three Other Greater Manchester Hospitals
articles.excerpt: Over 350 staff members from Rochdale Infirmary and three other hospitals will strike next week over a dispute regarding overtime management.
articles.content_html:
Hundreds of operating theatre staff are set to strike next week at four Greater Manchester hospitals, including Rochdale Infirmary. More than 350 employees, including nurses, clinical support workers, and housekeepers, will participate in the strike on Monday 24 August, Wednesday 26 August, and Friday 28 August.

The dispute centres on the Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust's (NCA) use of an outside agency, NHS Professionals (NHSP), to manage overtime. Trade union Unison claims that an offer made by NCA to resolve the dispute was withdrawn before discussions could occur. Kevin Dolan, Unison's North West regional organiser, stated that staff are simply asking for what their contracts entitle them to.

Gertie Nic Philib, the trust's chief people and strategy officer, acknowledged the staff's right to take lawful industrial action. Dolan expressed frustration over the lack of leadership from NCA, emphasising that the union is ready to negotiate but feels the trust has no intention of resolving the issue.

The strikes may impact services at Rochdale Infirmary and the other hospitals involved, potentially leading to delays or cancellations of scheduled procedures. Patients are advised to check with their healthcare providers for updates regarding their appointments during the strike dates.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers travelling towards and away from Manchester.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop is out of service as of 19 August 2026, impacting access for passengers. The disruption is expected to last until further notice, according to a travel alert from the Bee Network.

For those travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading away from Manchester can also use a ramp from Cromford Street, followed by a track crossing to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

The Bee Network has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption and encourages passengers to plan their journeys accordingly. Passengers are advised to check the Bee Network's live travel alerts for the latest information regarding the lift's status and any alternative arrangements that may be necessary.
